questions.q: Why does FBDI require data as CSV rather than uploading the Excel workbook directly?
options: Because Excel files are always too small
Because CSV files look nicer when opened
Because Oracle cannot read any Microsoft file formats
Because interface tables only care about raw column values, and CSV strips away formatting, formulas, and other structure the import doesn't need
questions.explain: CSV reduces a workbook to its essential data — rows and comma-separated values — which is exactly what an interface table load process needs and nothing more.

questions.q: How should the CSV files actually be generated from a populated FBDI template?
options: By manually re-typing the data into a plain text file
By using the macro button (e.g. 'Generate CSV File') on the template's Instructions tab
By using Excel's generic 'Save As CSV' option on each tab individually
CSV files are not needed at all — the Excel file is uploaded directly
questions.explain: The template's built-in macro guarantees the correct column order and formatting for each interface table. A generic Save As CSV cannot reliably reproduce this for multi-tab templates.

questions.q: If a template has two data tabs (e.g. invoice headers and invoice lines), what does generating the CSV files produce?
options: A single combined CSV file with both tabs merged together
No files at all, because two tabs is not supported
Two separate CSV files, one per data tab, because each tab maps to a separate interface table
An Excel file instead of a CSV
questions.explain: Each data tab corresponds to its own interface table, so each one generates its own CSV file.

questions.q: What has to happen to the generated CSV files before upload to UCM?
options: They must be bundled together into a single ZIP archive
They must be converted back into Excel format
They must be printed and faxed
Nothing — each CSV is uploaded individually, one at a time
questions.explain: The Load Interface File for Import process expects one ZIP archive containing all the CSVs that belong to that load, not separate loose files.

questions.q: A first-time user clicks 'Generate CSV File' and nothing happens. What is the most common cause?
options: The data itself is always wrong
The computer's clock is set to the wrong time zone
Oracle Fusion is down
Excel's macro security settings or Protected View are blocking the macro from running
questions.explain: Because CSV generation runs as a macro, Excel's security settings (and Protected View on downloaded files) commonly block it by default — this is the first thing to check, before assuming the data is broken.
